title: Lifting Loads
objective: Explain lifting concepts at knowledge level, recognise that standard communication, safety controls and approved load information govern lifting work, and understand why load-chart and working-load decisions belong within authorised occupational processes.

internal_assessment_criteria: IAC0401 — Identify and describe overhead-crane hand signals — 40%
IAC0402 — Identify and describe safety precautions, processes and equipment — 25%
IAC0403 — Interpret data from load charts — 15%
IAC0404 — Calculate and determine maximum working loads — 20%
curriculum_traceability.primary_source: QCTO occupational curriculum hosted by CHIETA — Curriculum-6.pdf

safety_boundary: Knowledge learning only. This lesson does not teach a learner to operate cranes, rig or sling loads, select lifting equipment for real work, direct a live lifting operation, or calculate a real-world safe lifting limit. Lifting work is hazardous and must be performed only through authorised occupational training or workplace processes under competent supervision and applicable controls.

sections.heading: 1. Lifting is controlled work
sections.body: Lifting work involves moving loads under controlled occupational conditions. At knowledge level, the learner should understand that lifting decisions depend on approved information, competent people, suitable equipment and established workplace controls rather than personal judgement or improvisation.

sections.heading: 2. Lifting concepts and methods
sections.body: The curriculum requires an understanding of lifting concepts and methods. In this Companion these are treated as theory: the learner recognises that different lifting situations require an authorised method matched to the task and controlled information. No operational lifting procedure is provided.

sections.heading: 3. Communication and hand signals
sections.body: Standardised communication is important because people involved in a lifting operation need a shared, unambiguous way to communicate. The curriculum requires learners to identify and describe overhead-crane hand signals. This lesson treats signals as recognition knowledge only and does not authorise anyone to direct crane operations.

sections.heading: 4. Safety precautions and controls
sections.body: Lifting work requires safety precautions, defined processes and appropriate equipment. Learners should understand the principle that hazards and controls must be addressed through the approved workplace system before lifting activity takes place. This lesson does not provide equipment-use instructions.

sections.heading: 5. Load charts are controlled information
sections.body: A load chart communicates limits and conditions for specified equipment. At knowledge level, learners should understand that chart information must be interpreted in its correct context and must never be guessed, assumed or transferred to unrelated equipment.

sections.heading: 6. Working-load calculations
sections.body: The curriculum includes calculating and determining maximum working loads. In this Companion, the learning boundary is conceptual: learners recognise that such determinations depend on verified data, specified conditions and approved occupational methods. This lesson does not provide formulas or calculations for use in live lifting operations.

sections.heading: 7. Stop when information is uncertain
sections.body: If required lifting information is missing, unclear, inconsistent or outside the learner's authorised role, the correct learning principle is to stop and refer the matter to the competent trainer or supervisor. Uncertainty must never be resolved by guessing.

sections.heading: 8. The learning boundary
sections.body: Understanding lifting terminology, communication, safety controls and controlled load information does not establish practical lifting competence. The Companion supports preparation for supervised training and formal assessment; it does not certify or authorise lifting work.

media.title: Planning and organising lifting operations
media.focus: Safety-focused theory reference explaining why lifting operations require competent planning, risk control, appropriate supervision and controlled work arrangements.
media.safety_scope: Use only for safety awareness and theory. This Companion does not use the resource to teach crane operation, rigging, slinging, live load calculation or practical lifting procedures.
